label: PLC 1x32 SC/APC connectorised shelf module
notes: The connectorised form of plc-1x32-sca: the same 1:32 PLC chip in an LGX/1RU shelf module with SC/APC adapters on the front, which is how a central-office or cabinet splitter shelf is actually bought. The chip figures are that row's, unchanged and from the same place: 15.05 dB ideal split (10*log10(32)) plus 2.05 dB excess = 17.1 dB, inside the band ITU-T G.671 sets for a 1x32 branching component on a normal-reach span (WR1, 13.3 dB min / 17.5 dB max - the band plc-1x32-sca quotes). Both chip numbers are typical values, the excess being the difference between the observed total and the ideal split, not a figure from a vendor sheet. What the termination changes is only the input: connectorised bills two SC/APC matings (the catalogue's own sc-apc row, 2 x 0.3 = 0.6 dB) where the spliced cassette bills one fusion splice (fusion, 0.1 dB), so this row reads 0.5 dB more ODN than the same chip spliced - the about 0.5 dB the spliced row's notes promise, and the two connectors the shelf input has. The trap when replacing this row, and it is the trap that matters at 1:32: a shelf module sheet prints ONE insertion-loss figure that already includes the module's own adapters - CommScope's LGX/1RU splitter guide gives 17.5 dB max for a 1x32 with connectors, PPC 17.0 dB, Gigalight 17.2 dB max for an LGX box, Corning 18.3 dB max - so that figure is compared against 15.05 + 2.05 + 0.6 = 17.7 dB and is never loaded into excessLossDb, which would charge the connectors twice. Read that way this row is 0.2 dB pessimistic against a module that meets WR1 with its connectors fitted; the pessimism is deliberate, because the engine can only express a chip figure plus separately charged matings. Why this row exists: the catalogue carried connectorised twins for 1x4, 1x8 and 1x16 (the NAP and splitter-box ratios) but not for 1x32, which is the ratio a CO shelf is built at, so the commonest connectorised splitter in a PON had no way to be drawn - a planner picked the spliced row and the BOM charged one splice and no patch field for a shelf of 32 adapters. The rest of the ladder stays spliced because buildPon resolves a splitter as plc-1x<ratio>-sca, so auto-design never picks this row: it is for a plant drawn by hand, or for a shelf whose cassettes arrive pre-terminated. Replace with the bought module's datasheet before construction.
